sanjay: Heads-up — seeing a p99 tail spike on prod since kernel-picker r12 rolled last night. p95 barely moved but p99 doubled for short-sequence traffic. Anyone else see this? :frowning:
perf-bot: perf summary (last 60m): baseline-window(24h before r12) p95=40ms p99=110ms; post-r12 p95=42ms p99=225ms. KV hit-rate stable ~87%.
tom: Can you dump a quick profile and the scheduler params for the affected pool? which model/route?
maria: Affected pool: text-gen-small (seq <=128), mostly microburst PLG traffic. Scheduler config (prod):
```
max_batch_tokens: 1024
max_wait_ms: 5
max_batch_items: 64
batching_strategy: continuous
```
maria: Also kernel-picker r12 changed the surface order: prefer fused-attn kernel when estimated seq*batch < 8192, else slowpath. That heuristic may be misestimating microbatch sizes due to prefix caching.
alex: If KV cache is returning prefixes, the runtime may be sending longer effective seq to kernel estimator (seq + kv_prefix_len) -> picks a kernel that has expensive cold-warm handshake for tails.
perf-bot: profiler dump (sample):
```
- 38% time: kernel:fused_attn_init (cold handshake)
- 26% time: wait_queue (microbatch coalescing)
- 18% time: kernel:fused_attn_exec
- 12% time: kv_prefetch
```
sanjay: Interesting — big fraction in fused_attn_init cold handshake. That suggests kernel warm path not being hit for many requests.
tom: Quick experiment idea: tune picker threshold to prefer warm path when estimated_tokens_per_microbatch < 2048, and increase max_wait_ms to 8ms for a limited cohort. Tradeoff: slightly higher p95 but lower p99.
maria: I ran two 10m experiments yesterday on staging with real trace replay:
- control (prod-like): max_wait_ms=5, picker-threshold=8192 => p95=42ms p99=230ms
- test A: max_wait_ms=8, picker-threshold=2048 => p95=48ms p99=140ms
- test B: max_wait_ms=3, picker-threshold=2048 => p95=39ms p99=260ms
Interpretation: increasing wait gives bigger microbatches which amortize kernel init overhead and reduce tail, at the cost of median latency up ~6ms.
alex: So we have classic latency SLO vs throughput/tail tradeoff. For interactive apps we want tight p95, but consumer PLG apps prefer p99 stability.
sanjay: Any quick mitigations we can push without full revert of r12?
maria: Short-term: bump picker to prefer warm path when estimated_tokens_per_microbatch < 4096 and enable aggressive warm-kernel prefetch for pools with >80% short seq traffic. Also temporarily roll max_wait_ms to 8ms on dedicated pools with SLO tuned for p99.
tom: Ops note: bumping max_wait_ms from 5->8 increased effective avg batch_tokens from ~600 -> ~1100 in staging; throughput improved ~12% and GPU kernel init count dropped ~45%.
perf-bot: staging numbers for test window (10m):
```
control: avg_batch_tokens=620, kernel_inits=1842
test: avg_batch_tokens=1120, kernel_inits=1010
```
ci-bot: small revert candidate created: PR #4825 (picker-threshold tweak + warm-prefetch flag). Can canary to 5% for 30m.
maria: Proposed canary plan:
- 5% user traffic -> apply picker-threshold=2048, max_wait_ms=8, warm_prefetch=true
- monitor p95/p99, kernel_init rate, kv hit latency
- rollback if gpu_init_count reduction <30% or p99 not improving
alex: Also add a microprofile hook to log estimated_tokens_used_by_picker vs actual_tokens_sent for 1% of requests so we can tune estimator.
sanjay: Sounds good. Can someone own the rollout? @maria? :thumbsup:
maria: I'll own canary. I'll also attach a flamegraph link and the staging perf traces to the PR.
tom: I'll prepare dashboard alerts for kernel_init rate (>20% change) and p99 delta > +30%.
sanjay: Thanks — let's reconvene after 30m canary. If green, we can widen to 25% then 100% over a day. :eyes:
maria: quick note: long-term we should consider decoupling kernel handshake from first exec (background warmers) and add a tiny prewarm budget in runtime to avoid cold init at tail.
alex: filing follow-up ticket for kernel prewarm and picker ML estimator (FP-723)
perf-bot: Alert scheduled: canary-run started at 2300123456
sanjay: OK closing thread for now — follow updates in PR #4825 and FP-723. Thanks team :rocket:
